synopsis: The cheapest early experiments are intended to falsify the collision-mitigation proposal before expensive infrastructure is built; Chapter 13 identifies sixteen experiments, each producing an artifact and a stopping or escalation signal [f10912, f16532, f16533]. Several can begin in October 2026 using existing warning-system data, historical tests, supplier discussions and one representative machine; parallel recording on current machines is identified as the single most valuable pre-hardware action, and winter 2026–2027 reference data should be captured before the season passes [f10914, f5574, f14351, f10953]. The proposed tests include checking supplier data and legal rights, replaying logs to estimate false activations, correlating one machine and scenario with simulation, and carrying one safety requirement through a real test, model, virtual result and residual-risk decision—the “golden thread,” described as the cheapest decisive experiment [f10915, f10925, f10930, f12195]. These tests must establish credible evidence rather than superficial similarity: weather simulation should reproduce measured sensor degradation, correlation should include residual plots and an uncertainty budget, and hand-made object-list tests provide no evidence that perception works [f10937, f16538, f12536]. Funding should be stage-gated around data availability, correlation, transfer to a materially different configuration and reviewer acceptance; unresolved supplier access, inadequate reference data or excessive bespoke tuning are explicit reasons to stop or escalate, while a published off-road shadow-mode protocol remains missing [f10746, f16550, f10918, f10956, f10948, f10929].
